turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call. Start with why Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class, before anyone called me.
Upset isn't the issue. Nobody called me, and my son sat in class and read his mark on his phone. Why was that the first he heard of it?
But I'm not changing the grade.
"Not changing it" is your position, not a reason. Who entered the zero, and on what basis?
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.
I'm writing that down: you're not changing it. Now answer the question. Who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.
Then the answer is that the zero went in before anyone heard from Owen or from me. Our school's procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark consequence is entered. Is that what happened?
